sources.title: Technical companion to Long runs and rare patterns of a random completely multiplicative function
sources.author: Brice Pouly
sources.role_in_batch: Companion of the target proof package; no complete appendix is claimed as formalized by this batch.

covered: Pointwise probability error in an adequate finite prime cylinder, with the actual defective-vertex count.
Exact uniform word probability for every fixed assignment of the small prime coordinates in the finite cylinder.
Measurable infinite word events and exact unconditional finite/infinite identities for their measures and real probabilities.
Pointwise real inequality (2.6) under the actual infinite Rademacher law, with no exposed cylinder cutoff.
Measurable infinite small-prime assignment atoms with explicit strictly positive finite mass for every assignment.
For Y <= M, the small-prime atom sigma-algebra is exactly the cylinder sigma-algebra of all prime signs at most Y (F_Y).
Exact infinite identity measure(word intersect atom) = measure(atom) / 2^B and conditional ratio 1 / 2^B under the odd-valuation good-window hypothesis.
Finite distinct-word occurrence count in the actual infinite model, integrability, and exact integral equal to the sum of word probabilities.
Finite summed probability error bounded by (dictionary cardinality / 2^B) times the total word defect weight.
Finite shifted-root defect comparison and uniform N^(1/2+o(1)) word defect mass in every fixed logarithmic band.
Dyadic summed probability and actual unconditional expectation clauses, with the threshold chosen before length, position mask and dictionary.

hypotheses: Every vertex x - 1 + j, j < B, has odd valuation at some prime strictly greater than Y.
infinite_conditional_endpoint.assignment: Every sigma : SmallSample M Y; its atom has positive finite source measure.

corollary_2_6.coverage_summary: The pointwise, conditional and dyadic summed clauses are proved through explicit infinite-probability, positive F_Y atom, and occurrence-integral representations.
optional_presentation_work: General conditional-expectation API repackaging of the proved positive-atom law, if useful; this is not a missing step in the summed first-moment result.
corollary_2_6.scope_boundary: The summed endpoints range over arbitrary finite masks within [N, 2N); no macroscopic extension beyond this dyadic domain is claimed.

summed_first_moment_endpoint.random_variable: wordOccurrenceCount B s W: the finite sum of infiniteWordEvent indicators over x in s and b in W.
summed_first_moment_endpoint.quantifiers: For every natural k > 0, there exists N0 such that for all N >= N0, all lengths B in the fixed logarithmic band, all finite masks s in [N,2N), and all finite dictionaries W of distinct B-bit words, the displayed expectation bound holds.
summed_first_moment_endpoint.logarithmic_band: c1 * log N <= B <= c2 * log N.
summed_first_moment_endpoint.conclusion: abs(integral(wordOccurrenceCount B s W) - card(s)*card(W)/2^B)^(2*k) <= (card(W)/2^B)^(2*k) * N^(k+1).
summed_first_moment_endpoint.dictionary_representation: Finset (Fin B -> F2), so words are distinct.

covered: Abstract two-parity nullity and finite relation-weight comparisons.
Actual two-window valuation matrix and separate block-parity maps.
Linear equivalence between the constrained full-value relation space and the actual two-start relation space.
Full-value relations characterized by square products, and nonzero nullity by a nonempty indexed square-product subset, under positivity and cylinder adequacy.
Identification of full-value hosts with unrestricted arithmetic square-product hosts, without either block-parity restriction.
Finite inequality (3.24) over actual ordered separated pairs, with the unrestricted arithmetic host correction.
Large-prime assignment for arbitrary full-value coefficients, without either block-parity restriction.
Unrestricted square-product hosts in any dyadic pair mask lie in the retained congruence certificate cover.
Explicit dyadic host bound 8 (L + 1) N sqrt(3N) exp(4 sqrt(L + 1)) for N >= 2 and L <= N.
Uniform dyadic N^(3/2+o(1)) host estimate over every pair mask in the dyadic square, with length- and mask-independent threshold in each fixed logarithmic band.
Unrestricted large-prime assignment and arithmetic host cover for arbitrary positive intervals [A,Z), without a bounded-ratio or block-parity hypothesis.
Finite global host count on every pair mask in [2,M]^2, followed by a uniform M^(3/2+o(1)) bound under only L+1 <= C*log M.
Exact macroscopic start interval [ceil(M^delta),M) and both host inequalities of Proposition 3.7, with cutoff M+L for start relations.
Uniform full-host bound normalized by the lower scale N on bounded-ratio intervals, with a threshold chosen before the upper endpoint M, length L and pair mask.
Exact natural macroscopic start/full-value weighted masses, with identical ordered separated pair masks and prime cutoff M+L.
Unconditional equality of the real start mass with the historical R2kappa interval mass, including empty populations.
Finite rational/residual decomposition for each historical canonical-code parameter A, under M >= 2 and delta > 0, without an endpoint-ratio condition.
Equation (3.24) specialized to the literal macroscopic masses and arithmetic full hosts.
Unconditional uniform M^(3/2+o(1)) bound on max(0, Rvalue - 4*Rstart), with threshold before L and delta.
The rational component of the raw profile is now independently covered through Proposition 3.8, keeping the distinct powers of Q_B; this does not yet establish the residual sectors or full (3.25).

finite_endpoint.parameters: M L : Nat; I : Finset Nat; word length B = L + 1
hypotheses: For every x in I, 2 <= x.
For every x in I, x + L <= M + 1.
finite_endpoint.pair_set: Ordered pairs (x,y) in I x I with L < Nat.dist x y.
finite_endpoint.host_meaning: A nonempty indexed subset of the full vertex occurrences has square product; no parity restriction in either block.

remaining: Theorem 3.1 raw relation profile and its combination with finite (3.24) to obtain asymptotic (3.25), with all stated uniformity.

dyadic_host_endpoint.quantifiers: For every real C >= 0 and natural k > 0, there exists N0 such that for all N >= N0, all admissible L, and every pair mask s in the dyadic square, card(squareProductHosts L s)^(2*k) <= N^(3*k+1).
dyadic_host_endpoint.mask: Any s subset of dyadicBlock N x dyadicBlock N.

global_host_endpoint.quantifiers: For every real C >= 0 and natural k > 0, there exists M0 such that for all M >= M0, every L with L+1 <= C*log M, and every pair mask s in [2,M]^2, card(squareProductHosts L s)^(2*k) <= M^(3*k+1).
global_host_endpoint.mask: Any s subset of Icc 2 M x Icc 2 M.

macroscopic_mass_endpoints.weights: Natural 2^rho - 1, with cast to real for the retained mass identity.
macroscopic_mass_endpoints.decomposition_scope: The exact finite decomposition of the historical canonical rational code for every parameter A. This does not identify all eight current sectors or establish their weighted estimates.

positive_correction_endpoint.quantifiers: For every fixed real C >= 0 and every natural k > 0, there exists M0 before all M >= M0, lengths L with L+1 <= C*log M, and real delta > 0.
positive_correction_endpoint.conclusion: max(0, (macroscopicValueMassNat M L delta : Real) - 4*(macroscopicStartMassNat M L delta : Real))^(2*k) <= M^(3*k+1).

additional_exclusions: The complete signed marked-field, dictionary, and two-source crossover theorems.

proposition_3_7.covered: Both H_start <= H_full and the uniform macroscopic H_full <= M^(3/2+o(1)) host bound.
proposition_3_7.interval: Ico (ceil(M^delta) in Nat) M, exactly the natural starts satisfying M^delta <= x < M.
proposition_3_7.pair_mask: Ordered pairs in the macroscopic interval with L < Nat.dist x y.
proposition_3_7.quantifiers: For each natural k > 0, there exists M0 before all M >= M0, lengths L with L+1 <= C*log M, and real delta > 0.
proposition_3_7.conclusion: card(startRelationHosts (M+L) L s) <= card(squareProductHosts L s) and card(squareProductHosts L s)^(2*k) <= M^(3*k+1).
proposition_3_7.cutoff: M+L, sufficient for all actual vertices.
proposition_3_7.note: The finite estimate uses 3M instead of 2M. It proves the same claimed macroscopic asymptotic bound. No raw weighted relation profile is asserted.

bounded_ratio_endpoint.quantifiers: For each natural k > 0, there exists N0 before all N >= N0, all upper endpoints M with N <= M <= kappa*N, all lengths L with L+1 <= C*log N, and all masks s in [2,M]^2.
bounded_ratio_endpoint.conclusion: card(squareProductHosts L s)^(2*k) <= N^(3*k+1). On the separated pair mask of [N,M), the start/full host comparison with cutoff M+L is proved jointly.

lemma_3_3_macroscopic.fixed_parameters: Real C >= 0 and delta > 0; coding parameter A = 3.
lemma_3_3_macroscopic.threshold: Chosen before length L and starts x,y, under L+1 <= C*log M. Depends on C and delta.
lemma_3_3_macroscopic.arithmetic_inequality: 4*((L+1)^3)^2*(L+1) < M^delta <= x for x in the macroscopic domain.
lemma_3_3_macroscopic.covered: At most one reduced candidate, selection of every available candidate, and equality of every nonzero primitive rational code with the canonical code, for an arbitrary prime cutoff.

covered: Finite actual rational masses filtered by canonical height exactly two and at least three, with weight 2^sigma - 1.
Exact partition of the total rational mass into these two filtered masses; lower heights have zero weight on separated pairs.
Finite independent bounds at the upper interval scale M, retaining the different exponents floor(L/2) and floor(L/3).
Exact finite support of every positive primitive geometry of height at least two and multiplicity m >= 2; binary geometry weight 2^(m-1), with no translation parameter.
All three uniform real-exponent inequalities (3.12)-(3.13), with Q_B = 2^(L+1) explicit.
A common threshold also guarantees the unique macroscopic canonical candidate for A=3.
proposition_3_8.quantifiers: There exists M0 depending only on C,delta,epsilon, such that for every M >= M0 and every L with L+1 <= C*log M all three inequalities and canonical uniqueness hold.
